title: Antenna length (468 / f)
idea: Lower frequency means a longer antenna. A half-wave dipole in feet is 468 divided by the frequency in MHz.

lines: Quarter wave (feet) = 234 / MHz, half of that
Yagi driven element ≈ a half wave
Reflector a bit longer, director a bit shorter
The whole dipole is the half wave; each side is half of it

compare.how: 468 / MHz feet end to end, fed in the middle.
234 / MHz feet tall. The ground or radials act as the other half.
Driven element about a half wave. Reflector behind is longer, director in front is shorter.

traps.why: 16 feet is one side. The whole dipole is 468 / 14.25 = 33 feet.
That's a full wave. A half wave is 468 / 3.55 = 132 feet.
That's a half wave (468 / 28.5). A quarter wave uses 234: 8 feet.

traps.wrong: The reflector is shorter, and the director is longer
traps.why: Backward. The reflector sits behind and is longer; the director points the way and is shorter.
